description: The Title 17 process to become a Regional Center provider via the Provider Directory portal.

sections.title: Experience Requirements
sections.summary: Minimum direct service experience requirements for administrators working with individuals with developmental disabilities based on the Regional Center service level.

bullets.label: Level 2
bullets.detail: At least 6 months of direct experience working with individuals with developmental disabilities is required. Level 2 facilities are not currently being pursued.

bullets.label: Level 3
bullets.detail: At least 9 months of direct experience working with individuals with developmental disabilities is required.

bullets.label: Level 4 5 and 6 (Formerly 4i)
bullets.detail: At least 12 months of direct experience working with individuals with developmental disabilities is required.

sections.title: Vendorization Training Requirements
sections.summary: Training and certifications commonly required for ARF administrators during licensing and Regional Center vendorization.

bullets.label: ARF Administrator Certification (ICTP)
bullets.detail: The administrator must complete a CDSS-approved 35-hour Initial Certification Training Program (ICTP) for Adult Residential Facilities and pass the administrator certification exam.

bullets.label: Residential Support Specialist (RSS 1)
bullets.detail: RSS 1 provides foundational training on supporting individuals with developmental disabilities in residential settings, including person-centered planning, documentation, and regulatory expectations required by the Regional Center.

bullets.label: Residential Support Specialist (RSS 2)
bullets.detail: RSS 2 expands on RSS 1 and focuses on advanced residential support strategies, behavioral support implementation, and compliance with Title 17 service delivery standards.

bullets.label: Positive Behavior Supports (PBS) Part 1 and 2
bullets.detail: PBS training focuses on understanding and implementing behavior support strategies for individuals with challenging behaviors. This training is typically required for higher service levels (such as Level 3 and Level 6). Equivalent qualifications may include certification as a BCBA or BCaBA.

bullets.label: Direct Support Professional Training (DSPT 1 & 2)
bullets.detail: DSPT provides foundational competency training for staff supporting individuals with developmental disabilities, covering health and safety, rights, communication, and daily living support. Administrators often complete this training to understand DSP competency requirements.

bullets.label: Residential Provider Orientation
bullets.detail: An orientation provided by the Regional Center that introduces new residential providers to vendorization expectations, reporting requirements, service coordination processes, and compliance with Title 17 regulations.

sections.title: Provider Directory Intake & Portal Workflow
sections.summary: The digital process for submitting the vendor application, program design, and securing final approval through the Regional Center's portal.

bullets.label: Requirements Stage Intake
bullets.detail: Submit initial vendor and applicant information, service location details, and the facility license in the Provider Directory to verify minimum requirements are met. The Regional Center has 15 calendar days to process this stage.

bullets.label: Program Design Submission
bullets.detail: During the Submission Stage, which carries a 30-calendar-day processing timeframe, upload the comprehensive Program Design detailing the service model, staffing ratios, and consumer support strategies.

bullets.label: System-Generated DS Forms
bullets.detail: The Provider Directory automatically generates drafts of the Vendor Application (DS 1890) and Applicant/Vendor Disclosure Statement (DS 1891). Review, modify the DS 1891 if needed, and execute them via electronic signature.

bullets.label: Decision Stage & Vendor Agreement
bullets.detail: Upload the Vendor Agreement as part of the Vendorization Checklist. The Regional Center has 45 days in the Decision Stage to render an approval or denial and issue the unique Vendor ID.
